chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among the rights of the one entering upon the people of the house is that they walk with him gently/slowly when he enters and when he leaves.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you enters upon his Muslim brother in his house, he is the commander over him until he goes out.'.

key_terms.أَمِيرٌ: Commander, leader, or one in charge

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a guest visiting a Muslim's home according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the social etiquette of visiting, where the host's gentle accompaniment signifies respect and the guest's temporary 'authority' underscores the sanctity of the home during the visit. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) in interpersonal relationships, balancing humility with honor. The concept of the guest's precedence aligns with the Prophetic tradition of treating visitors as a trust from God.
